samir-runtime: FYI — after the runtime v2.43 deploy we're seeing a host-side CPU regression on ingress for short chat requests (<50 tokens). p50 host CPU increased ~12% on the canary.
samir-runtime: Traces/Flame show hotspots in tokenization, request parsing and a lot of small syscalls from the streaming path (lots of tiny writes).
samir-runtime: Quick excerpt from `perf` aggregated flame:
```
34.1% tokenization.cpp:Tokenize::run
18.7% http_parser.c:execute
12.3% writev
8.0% sendto
5.6% kv_cache.cpp:lookup
4.5% memcpy
```
samir-runtime: The streaming path currently does: parse -> tokenize -> build chunk -> flush per-chunk (2-3 small buffers). That yields many syscalls per request which kills host CPU under high QPS.
marie-ml: ran a local microbench with small messages and a tiny change: reuse tokenizer instances + buffer reuse (tokenizer pool). Result: host CPU median dropped from 29% -> 20% at same load. Syscalls per req dropped ~14%.
marie-ml: quick numbers (5k req/s short msgs): before: host CPU 29%, p50 latency 22ms. after (tokenizer pool): host CPU 20%, p50 21ms.
joseph-sre: are we doing write() or writev? If it's write() per buffer that's N syscalls. We should coalesce to writev or use a short coalescing window + writev. Also consider TCP_CORK / TCP_NOPUSH on the egress path.
samir-runtime: code path is currently constructing a vector of small iovecs and calling sendmsg/sendto per chunk. We can change to an aggregator: accumulate up to N iovecs or X bytes then single writev. Also add heuristic: if we see client expecting early flush (low streaming-latency SLO) skip coalesce.
elaine-devex: need to be mindful of client expectations — some SDKs rely on immediate partials. Make coalescing configurable with default conservative behavior. SDKs should expose `streaming.coalesce=true|false` and runtime can have an override flag.
marie-ml: did a short experiment: tokenizer pool + per-conn slab (bounded 8KB) + writev coalesce (max 4KB or 6 chunks) reduced host cpu by additional 6% vs tokenizer-pool only. End-to-end: host CPU 14% lower than baseline, p50 latency unchanged or slightly better.
marie-ml: bench command I used: `./bench/ingress_small_msgs.sh --clients 200 --msgs 5000 --payload <= 40B`
marie-ml: perf smoke output (post-change):
```
23.0% tokenization.cpp:Tokenize::run
9.9% http_parser.c:execute
6.4% writev
4.1% kv_cache.cpp:lookup
```
joseph-sre: watch interactions with KV cache key generation — if we reuse token buffers we must ensure we don't retain references that prevent proper cache eviction or blow memory.
samir-runtime: plan:
  1) land tokenizer pool PR (tokenize reuse + buffer pool)
  2) implement writev coalescing with an opt-in runtime flag (default: enabled with conservative thresholds)
  3) add telemetry: per-conn syscall_count, avg_iov_per_send, coalesce_hit_rate
  4) canary in us-west-2 for 24h, measure host CPU and p50/p95 latencies
elaine-devex: I'll update quickstart and SDK notes to show how to toggle `streaming.coalesce` and document the compatibility caveats. Will also add a short migration guide for teams relying on early flush semantics.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout plan created: runtime v2.44 / branch `opt/tokenizer-pool-io-coalesce` — canary group: ingress nodes in us-west-2. PR: #4021
dev-bot: CI: opt/tokenizer-pool green (unit + perf-smoke). Perf suite: ./ci/perf/smoke_ingress_short.sh passed.
samir-runtime: joseph, marie — can you both +1 the coalesce thresholds? I'm thinking default max_coalesce_bytes=4096, max_coalesce_iovs=6, max_latency_ms=3 (linger short window) so we avoid perceptible streaming delay.
joseph-sre: +1 on those defaults. Add a kill-switch env var and metric to track cases where coalesce caused client-visible slowdowns.
marie-ml: +1 — I'll add an A/B to compare coalesce=true vs false with real traffic patterns.
samir-runtime: okay landing plan: tokenizer pool PR first (small risk), then IO coalesce behind flag. I'll drop a short summary + perf numbers in #eng-runtime after 24h canary. tagging @marie-ml @joseph-sre @elaine-devex :eyes:
